Ruling: batch #167 item 3 · letter B (the render path is not a validation door, and is declared so: the doors are the framework's load-time zod parse — `content/docs/guide/metadata-diagnostics.md:9` — and the authoring-side `objectui validate` / `objectui check` / `safeValidateSchema`; one short section lands in `content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md` and one line in `SchemaRenderer`'s comment beside the `__DEV__` guard; the dev-only structural walker stays as it is) · maintainer 「其他同意」 2026-09-18T15:17Z

Director seat, summon #24, `session_01Wj1HUjzyeiBQ8atRf1ZhaL`. Presented in detail with the recommendation B; the maintainer agreed.

Why B: mainstream UI runtimes validate props in development only and trust the document at render; metadata platforms validate at save / load, not at paint. This platform already has both doors — every metadata document is parsed against its zod schema when the framework loads it (Studio surfaces the result), and an author who runs `objectui validate` / `check` is refused with the retirement's own message. A third door, per render, in the browser, adds cost to every paint and catches nothing a served document has not already passed. The card's finding stands and is why the text is owed: the retirement is delivered where documents are authored and checked, ⛔ not where they are rendered, and no published text says so today.

⛔ A (wire the zod root parse into `SchemaRenderer`): refused, above. ⛔ A dev-only zod parse: a feature, not a stability fix; if wanted it is a new card, ⛔ not a rider here. ⛔ The render-time refusal the card documents for a record-shaped `body` (refused for `schema.children.type`, never for the retirement) is not made to "agree": it is named in the text as the accidental coverage it is, so nobody reads it as enforcement.

## Execution

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; labels stay (`domain:spec`, `priority:p2`). Deliverable is text only: (i) `content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md` gains a short section 「Render is not a validation door」 naming the three doors and stating that a production build validates nothing at render; (ii) the comment at the `SchemaRenderer.tsx:73` `__DEV__` guard says the same in one line and points at the doc. No code path changes; Clause-②: no. The dispatch-template conflict the card records (a dev told to file a card) is carried on the os-dev.md family, not here.

## ⚠️ 前提过时检查 —— one hit, declared

`origin/main` is **`f156329bb5`** (read at 2026-09-19T02:55Z; ⛔ a moved tip is never a landing). Since this card was filed, **`2acd8e109c` (PR objectui#9895) landed and retired the `body` child-list dialect**.

⭐ That matters because **the card's reproduction used a retired `body` key on a `chatbot` node as its probe**. The card's *claim* — that the render path never consults the zod root parse, and that in a production build nothing validates — is ⛔ not about `body`; `body` was only the instrument. But the instrument itself has now moved.

⇒ The dev is instructed to **re-take the reading on current `main` before writing a word of the new text**, and to report honestly if the old probe is now dead rather than reproducing a stale reading. ⚠️ If the re-take shows the render path's behaviour is no longer what the card describes, that is a **stop-and-hand-back**, ⛔ not a prose adjustment: the text owed depends on the behaviour being what letter B says it is.

The two doors the text must name are `content/docs/guide/metadata-diagnostics.md:9` (the framework's load-time zod parse) and the authoring side (`objectui validate` / `objectui check` / `safeValidateSchema`) — both to be verified at head, ⛔ not quoted from this comment.
